title: Playback data in the Dashboard
lead: Compare playback quality by browser or device in the Dashboard and inspect affected sessions. Use Grafana for custom charts and retain their query settings.

blocks.text: Compare browsers or devices in the Dashboard

items: In Bitmovin Dashboard Observability, select the collector’s Analytics license.

Select a fixed period containing the playback and retain its time zone and filters. Open the Video Startup Time browser breakdown and check Video Starts too. Distinguish a few slow playbacks from a broadly affected audience.
Keep the metric and period fixed while changing one device, platform or browser condition at a time.
Compare Rebuffering Percentage and Error Percentage for the same population. Use the Query API for dimensions or aggregations unavailable in the view.

blocks.text: Browser identifies the browser family, Device Class categories such as desktop, phone or tablet, and Device Type a model or device type. Dashboard breakdowns cover only some API fields; check the available choices.
Narrow an error down to a session

items: Inspect error types and frequency in Top Errors, using the license, period and content filters for the playback under investigation.
Open an associated session and check its code, Player, OS and event time.
Read Errors in the session details. Descriptions and additional data depend on the collector and platform.
Match the playback and time with the app log to investigate settings, network and content. An error description alone is not a complete diagnosis.

Choose a chart for the question

rows: Did quality change during the day?
A time series with consistent time buckets; separate browser series if needed.
Start/end, time zone, interval, metric, aggregation and filters.
Which browser or device needs attention?
A category table or bar chart over the whole period, accompanied by the relevant session/start count.
Group-by field, ordering, limit and the population represented by each category.
What is the value for the whole period?
A total or scorecard without time buckets.
The whole-range aggregation, not an unweighted average of chart points.

blocks.text: Averaging hourly medians or percentages from unequal groups does not give the whole-period value. Query that period again and retain its population counts. Distinguish missing data from a measured zero.
Read the metric and its population

items.label: Definitions and units for Plays, startup, buffering and errors

blocks.text: API durations use milliseconds; the Dashboard may format them as seconds. Label converted units in the chart title or axis. A change from 2% to 3% is 1 percentage point and a 50% relative increase.
Build a custom view with Grafana
The official Bitmovin Grafana Plugin instructions target self-managed Grafana. Configure its data source with the API key and Analytics license. Keep the API key out of Player Lab’s browser settings.

items: Create a panel with Bitmovin Analytics as its data source. Select the aggregation, dimension and any filters.
For trends, enable Format as time series, choose an Interval such as AUTO, and optionally Group By browser to produce separate series.
For a category table, disable Format as time series, add Group By and use an explicit order and limit. Retain the query definition with the dashboard.

blocks.text: Keep data and query settings together

rows: Displays result rows without chart building or CSV/JSON download buttons. See Analytics API queries for execution and response details.
Save aggregate JSON with its license label, start/end, aggregation, field, interval, filters, groupBy, order and limit. Exclude authentication headers from the analysis file.

A separate API workflow exports raw CSV or Parquet to S3, GCS or Azure. Specify the period, output and columns, then check task status. This differs from an aggregate query response or Player Lab download.

blocks.text: rows and rowCount do not describe column meanings or units. Retain those with the original query before charting the result. Raw exports may contain session data; prepare a limited aggregate before sharing with an LLM.
